title: incremental-typed-payloads-and-sdk-attachment-protocol-wip
content:
Context and motivation:

This doc captures an early PRD sketch for a lightweight incremental payload format and a companion SDK attachment protocol. The goal: let hosted-api streaming responses include typed "attachments" (large blobs, structured tables, execution receipts, tool outputs) that are both easy for clients to consume incrementally and cheap to route through the stream gateway.

Why this matters:
- Customers building interactive UIs and tool-enabled agents want structured subdocuments (e.g., a CSV extract, an evaluation scorecard, or runnable code) delivered as first-class parts of the stream without blocking the main text generation path.
- Large attachments today are either inlined (bloats tokens & latency) or referenced via separate upload flows (fragile UX).
- A typed incremental payload + SDK contract can standardize client behavior: progressive display, resumable downloads, integrity checks, and graceful truncation.

High-level goals (MVP):
- A minimal, backward-compatible streaming envelope that can carry small typed payloads in-band and larger attachments out-of-band with progressive anchors.
- SDK ergonomics: provide a simple Attachment object with streaming iterators in JS/Python, auto-retry, checksum validation, and an option for lazy fetch vs. immediate inline expand.
- Server-side: gateway-level lightweight dedup + CDN offload for attachments; support ephemeral URLs with short TTLs and integrity metadata.
- Observability: token/attachment-level telemetry so we can correlate attachment size/latency with UX regressions.

Non-goals (for MVP):
- Full content-addressed storage or a permanent file store.
- Arbitrary large file streaming (>100MB) is out-of-scope initially — focus on up to ~10MB blobs and chunked delivery patterns.

User stories:
1) Product engineer embedding a summarization widget sees a progressive table appear while the text completes; the table arrives as an attachment streamed in chunks and the UI can render rows as they arrive.
2) An agent runtime calls a tool; the tool returns a JSON result too big to inline. The SDK receives an Attachment handle and streams the JSON for downstream parsing.
3) Mobile client with bandwidth constraints opts for attachment metadata only (title + size + preview) and fetches content on-demand.

Requirements (functional):
- Envelope framing: typed frames for the main text tokens and typed attachment frames. Each attachment frame includes: id, kind, size_estimate, checksum (sha256 hex), preview (optional small snippet), and resume_cursor.
- Chunked attachment chunks: chunks labeled with id and sequence index. Server should accept chunk-level resume tokens.
- Attachment URLs: short-lived (default 2 minutes) signed URLs served by CDN, indicated in the stream when content is complete or for large attachments that bypass in-band streaming.
- SDK: Attachment abstraction exposing async iterator (JS) / generator (Python) that yields bytes or decoded typed pieces (e.g., JSON objects, CSV rows).
- Backpressure: SDK must expose a simple buffer_limit parameter and a callback for slow consumers.
- Integrity: SDK validates checksum on complete receipt. In case of mismatch, caller sees a well-defined error that includes the resume_cursor so it can request missing chunks.

Operational constraints:
- Gateway must limit total concurrent in-band attachments per session (default max 3) and throttle oversized attachments to signed-URL offload.
- Logging: emit an attachment_start and attachment_complete event with sizes, latency, and failure reasons.
- Costing: attachments count toward attachment-data units (new billing dimension) distinct from token billing.

API sketch (streaming snippets) — pseudo protocol frames:

Main text frame (streamed as before):
{ "frame_type": "text_delta", "delta": "...partial text..." }

Attachment start frame (small attachment in-band):
{
  "frame_type": "attachment_start",
  "attachment": {"id":"a-42","kind":"table.csv","size_estimate":12000, "checksum":"sha256:abcd...", "preview":"col1,col2\n1,2\n"}
}

Attachment chunk frame:
{ "frame_type":"attachment_chunk", "id":"a-42", "seq": 0, "bytes_b64": "..." }

Attachment complete frame:
{ "frame_type":"attachment_complete", "id":"a-42", "checksum":"sha256:abcd..." }

Large-attachment-offload (when content too large to stream in-band) — announced in-stream as: 
{ "frame_type":"attachment_offload", "attachment": {"id":"a-99","kind":"tool-output.json","size":5242880, "signed_url":"https://cdn.redwood/....?sig=...","expires_at":"2025-11-05T15:21:00Z","checksum":"sha256:ef01..."} }

SDK ergonomics (JS example):
const att = await response.attachments.get('a-42');
for await (const chunk of att.iterChunks({bufferLimit: 64*1024})) {
  // chunk: Uint8Array or decoded row depending on parser
  ui.appendRows(parseCsv(chunk));
}
await att.ensureComplete(); // throws if checksum mismatch

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- In-band small attachments keep latency tight and simplify developer mental model, but they increase tokenization complexity if we attempt to treat content as text tokens — we avoid tokenizing attachments and treat them as binary payloads attached to stream frames.
- Signed-URL offload avoids gateway memory pressure for large blobs but adds a second fetch and potential UX race; SDK should handle optimistic prefetch when the client is on good bandwidth.
- Checksum validation is mandatory for tool outputs used by automated pipelines. For previews or lossy attachments (images with thumbnails), checksum can be optional.

Telemetry and evaluation:
- Instrument attachment lifecycle (start, first-byte, last-byte, complete/failed) with labels: kind, size_bucket, route, model, customer_tier.
- Add attachment-level SLOs: p50/p95 latency-to-first-byte and completion success rate.
- Create small playbooks for debugging checksum mismatches (common causes: truncation in transit, botched base64, encoding mismatch).

Edge cases and open questions:
- Should attachments be reference-counted across sessions to avoid duplicate storage? (defer: out of scope)
- Resume semantics for signed-URL offload—should we issue range headers or chunked downloads? (prefer range headers; SDK should expose resume cursor).
- Cross-model compatibility: attachments produced by a tool-run on a specific model version — do we need model version metadata? (add optional model_version field)
- How does this intersect with private deployments (VPC) where CDN offload may be disallowed? (must support in-band-only fallback and enterprise toggle).

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0: internal SDK + experimental gateway flag. Only used by Redwood-runner and internal QA.
- Phase 1: opt-in beta for specific customers with SDK 0.12+; provide a compatibility shim for older clients that will see attachment_offload frames as plain text URLs.
- Phase 2: default-on for hosted-api — telemetry-backed safety checks for gateway memory and customer error rates.

Backwards compatibility: clients that do not understand attachment frames will ignore unknown frame_type values and see only text deltas. However, attachment_offload frames must include a plain-text preview field to avoid silent data loss for legacy UIs.

Implementation notes for infra/serving-runtime:
- Add a small attachment queue per connection. Chunking boundary default 64KB.
- Gateway will attempt in-band streaming for attachments < 1MB and offload larger ones automatically. Configurable thresholds per customer.
- Storage: short-term object store with 10-minute TTL for signed URLs; attachment metadata persisted in request logs for audit.

Next steps and action items:
- Product: finalize API fields and agree on attachment size thresholds (decision: default in-band <= 1MB, configurable).
- SDK: prototype JS & Python Attachment iterators and resume logic (owner: Noah).
- Infra: experiment with signed-url flow using CDN and measure p50 fetch latency from our major regions (owner: Oliver).
- Applied ML: define tool-output schema guidance and a small set of standard kinds (json, table.csv, image.png) (owner: Priya).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and errs on the side of pragmatic defaults rather than a fully generalized file-store. Please comment on the attachment frame fields and SDK surface area; sample code can be expanded into a canonical SDK PR once we agree on resume & checksum semantics.

Unresolved: default billing implications (attachment-data units granularity) and whether preview snippets should be auto-generated server-side or required from the tool/model runtime.

Scratchpad (brainstorm fragments):
- idea: attachments with small TTL caches in SDK to avoid refetch on quick replays.
- idea: allow server to send "delta-json" attachments where each chunk is a JSON patch applied by client. Useful for incremental tables.
- note: ensure we never leak signed URLs into logs that customers treat as persistent links.

End of draft.
